advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make check_cache_effective distinguish an empty/absent usage_rows input from a genuinely-uncached run (raise or return an explicit 'unmeasured' state).
evidence: ABSENCE: no test exercises check_cache_effective([]) — empty input is neither guarded nor covered.
advisory.finding: check_cache_effective fails open: an empty usage_rows list returns {"cached": False, "first_cache_hit_row": None}, which is indistinguishable from a run that genuinely had no cache hits versus a run whose usage log was never emitted/collected. The function never asserts the producer ran (non-empty rows / a liveness signal) before deriving its 'not cached' verdict.
scenarios: usage-log rows were never populated (upstream capture failed) yet the run is reported as 'not cached' rather than as an unmeasurable/empty condition
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard the empty case up front, e.g. `if not usage_rows: raise ValueError("no usage rows to classify — cache-effectiveness is unmeasurable")`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document or fix the `i >= 1` skip in check_cache_effective — justify why row 0 cache reads are excluded, or count them.
evidence: ABSENCE: no comment or test justifies why row 0 cache reads are deliberately excluded; the docstring only says it 'classifies a run's usage-log rows as cached/uncached'.
advisory.finding: check_cache_effective ignores a cache hit on the FIRST row (index 0): the guard `if i >= 1` means a run whose only cache_read_tokens>0 row is row 0 is reported cached=False. If row 0 can ever legitimately carry cache_read_tokens>0, this silently under-reports cache effectiveness.
scenarios: a warm-start run whose very first logged row already reads from a pre-existing cache

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a check_cache_effective test with a cache-read hit on row 0 (e.g. `[{"cache_read_tokens": 800}]`) asserting `cached is False` / `first_cache_hit_row is None`.
evidence: Named violating input: `check_cache_effective([{"cache_read_tokens": 800}])` returns `{"cached": False, "first_cache_hit_row": None}` per the added `i >= 1` guard, but no test asserts this — the two existing tests use all-zero reads (test_check_cache_effective_marks_uncached_when_zero_reads) and a hit at index 1 (test_check_cache_effective_marks_cached_on_later_hit).
ABSENCE: no test passes a single-row list, nor a list whose only cache_read_tokens>0 sits at index 0, so the row-0 exclusion behavior is unverified.
advisory.finding: check_cache_effective's `i >= 1` boundary — which deliberately treats a cache-read hit on the FIRST usage row (index 0) as uncached — is untested. The two tests cover only all-zero rows and a hit on row 1; none drives a row-0 hit, so removing or altering the `i >= 1` guard (a plausible refactor/regression) would go undetected.
scenarios: A refactor drops the `i >= 1` guard and starts counting a first-row cache hit as effective caching; the suite stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix:
def test_check_cache_effective_ignores_first_row_hit():
    verdict = parity.check_cache_effective([{"cache_read_tokens": 800, "cache_write_tokens": 0}])
    assert verdict["cached"] is False
    assert verdict["first_cache_hit_row"] is None

evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/parity.py:98-102: `def check_cache_effective(usage_rows: list[dict]) -> dict:` loops `if i >= 1 and row.get("cache_read_tokens", 0) > 0` then returns `{"cached": False, "first_cache_hit_row": None}` as the fall-through
ABSENCE: tests test_check_cache_effective_* cover only a 2-row uncached fixture and a 2-row later-hit fixture; no test exercises `[]` or a single-row list, so the empty-input verdict is unspecified

Litmus: the {cached: False} verdict is produced both when the run ran and read no cache AND when usage_rows is empty because telemetry never arrived — the check cannot distinguish its verdict from its own non-execution
advisory.finding: check_cache_effective fails open on empty or single-element usage_rows: an empty list (the producer emitted no usage telemetry) or a single row both return {"cached": False, "first_cache_hit_row": None} — identical to a genuinely-run-but-uncached verdict. A caller folding this into a report/ledger cannot distinguish 'cache was checked and found ineffective' from 'no usage rows were ever captured / the run produced no telemetry'.

evidence: tests assert only a no-read case and a hit-at-row-1 case (test_plan_replay_parity.py:197, :207); no test drives a cache_read at index 0 nor an empty usage_rows list
ABSENCE: the `i >= 1` first-row-exclusion branch is regression-blind — removing the guard (so row 0 counts) leaves every existing check_cache_effective test green
advisory.finding: check_cache_effective's `i >= 1` guard — which deliberately excludes a cache read appearing in the FIRST usage row (index 0) from counting as a cache hit — is newly added behavior with no test. The named violating input `[{"cache_read_tokens": 800}]` (a single row carrying a cache read) returns `{"cached": False, "first_cache_hit_row": None}`, and if the `i >= 1` guard were removed or changed to `i >= 0` no test would fail. The empty-list input `[]` is also untested.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_check_cache_effective_ignores_first_row_hit` with `rows=[{"cache_read_tokens": 800}]` asserting `cached is False`, and `test_check_cache_effective_empty_rows` with `rows=[]` asserting `cached is False, first_cache_hit_row is None`.

coaching.subject: temp-dir accumulation in repeated resolve_pinned_model calls

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Serialize the ephemeral rebar.toml with a TOML writer (or escape the model string) instead of raw f-string interpolation.
evidence: resolved comes from resolve_class -> _resolve_target which composes arbitrary provider:model strings (model_classes.py:298-304)
dropped.finding: resolve_pinned_model interpolates the resolved model string directly into a TOML document via an f-string without escaping; a resolved id containing a double-quote or backslash would produce a malformed rebar.toml that fails (or, worse, subtly mis-parses) when the eval caller's LLMConfig reads it.
scenarios: a future/custom Bedrock model id or endpoint-qualified string containing a quote or backslash

evidence: `resolved` originates from `resolve_class` over config-derived provider:model strings (model_classes.py:298), not a fixed literal
dropped.finding: resolve_pinned_model interpolates the resolved model id into a TOML document via naive f-string quoting: `{class_name} = {{ model = "{resolved}", fallback = [] }}`. If `resolved` (or class_name) ever contained a double quote or backslash, the emitted rebar.toml would be malformed or the value silently altered. Bedrock ids are safe in practice, but the round-trip is unvalidated.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Memoize the ephemeral config root per (class_name, resolved) or reuse a single temp dir across calls in resolve_pinned_model.
dropped.finding: resolve_pinned_model creates a new temp directory and registers a new atexit handler on every call, with no cleanup or memoization; repeated invocations (e.g. per-ticket in a corpus replay) accumulate temp dirs and atexit callbacks for the process lifetime.
scenarios: an eval harness that calls resolve_pinned_model once per pass per ticket across a large corpus run
